rows.speaker: عثمان بن أبي العاص الثقفي وأنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Uthman ibn Abi al-As and Anas, as well as Abu Hanifa and his companions, hold that fasting while traveling is better for one able to bear it.
rows.anchor: روي عن عثمان بن أبي العاص الثقفي وأنس بن مالك صاحبي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنهما قالا: الصوم في السفر أفضل لمن قدر عليه

words: يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ بِكُمُ ٱلْيُسْرَ وَلَا يُرِيدُ بِكُمُ ٱلْعُسْرَ
rows.speaker: ابن عمر وابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Umar, Ibn Abbas, and the other listed authorities hold that taking the travel concession and breaking the fast is preferable, citing God's intent of ease.
rows.anchor: روي عن ابن عمر وابن عباس: الرخصة أفضل، وقال به سعيد بن المسيب والشعبي وعمر بن عبد العزيز

rows.speaker: جمهور العلماء
rows.claim: The majority say that an ill resident unable to fast when the community fasted a 29-day Ramadan makes up 29 days.
rows.anchor: والجمهور من العلماء على أن أهل البلد إذا صاموا تسعة وعشرين يوما وفي البلد رجل مريض

rows.speaker: الحسن بن صالح بن حي
rows.claim: Hasan ibn Salih ibn Hayy says the person makes up a whole month for a whole month, without matching the number of days.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم منهم الحسن بن صالح بن حي: إنه يقضي شهرا بشهر من غير مراعاة عدد الأيام

rows.speaker: الكيا الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Kiya rejects making up a full month regardless of length: the verse requires a count of days, so missed days must be replaced day for day.
rows.anchor: قال الكيا الطبري: وهذا بعيد لقوله تعالى: { فعدة من أيام أخر } ولم يقل فشهر من أيام أخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause omits an understood condition: whoever among you is ill or traveling and breaks the fast must make it up.
rows.anchor: في الكلام حذف أي من يكن منكم مريضا أو مسافرا فأفطر فليقض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿIdda is nominative as the predicate of an omitted subject, with the sense that the ruling or duty is a counted number of days.
rows.anchor: ارتفع «عدة» على خبر الابتداء، تقديره فالحكم أو فالواجب عدة

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisa'i allows ʿidda to be read as an implied imperative: let the person fast a number of other days.
rows.anchor: وقال الكسائي: ويجوز فعدة أي فليصم عدة من أيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parse supplies the omitted noun ṣiyām, with ʿidda standing in its place.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المعنى فعليه صيام عدة فحذف المضاف وأقيمت العدة مقامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿIdda is a count or counted amount, like ṭaḥn for what is ground; the same noun is used for a woman's waiting period.
rows.anchor: والعدة فعلة من العد، وهي بمعنى المعدود كالطحن بمعنى المطحون

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh says ukhar is indeclinable because it is an adjectival form shifted from the form normally used with the definite article.
rows.anchor: لم ينصرف «أخر» عند سيبويه، لأنها معدولة عن الألف واللام

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisa'i derives ukhar from akhar by analogy with ḥamrāʾ and ḥumr, explaining its indeclinability.
rows.anchor: وقال الكسائي: هي معدولة عن آخر، كما تقول: حمراء وحمر فلذلك لم تنصرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that ukhar is indeclinable because it has a plural pattern while describing days; ukhrā was avoided lest it seem to modify ʿidda.
rows.anchor: وقيل: منعت من الصرف لأنها على وزن جمع وهي صفة لأيام ولم تجىء أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation derives ukhar as the plural of ukhrā, as in the expanded form ayyāmun ukhrā.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن { أخر } جمع أخرى كأنه أيام أخرى ثم كثرت فقيل: أيام أخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further explanation says days take a feminine adjective, accounting for the form ukhar.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن نعت الأيام يكون مؤنثا فلذلك نعتت بأخر

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports that “consecutive” was revealed after “a number of other days” and later dropped; al-Daraqutni grades the chain sound.
rows.anchor: فروي عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت: نزلت «فعدة من أيام أخر متتابعات» فسقطت «متتابعات» قال هذا إسناد صحيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier concession is removed by the command to fast, except for those unable to do so.
rows.anchor: فمن شهد منكم الشهر فليصمه [البقرة: 185] فزالت الرخصة إلا لمن عجز منهم

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says the pronoun in yutīqūnahu may refer to fasting: those able to fast could feed if they broke it, but this was abrogated by “that you fast.”
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: الضمير في «يطيقونه» يجوز أن يعود على الصيام

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra also allows the pronoun to refer to fidya, yielding the sense that those able to pay ransom owe a ransom.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يعود على الفداء أي وعلى الذين يطيقون الفداء فدية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading yuṭawwaqūnahu means being burdened with fasting despite hardship, as with the sick or pregnant; fasting suffices, while paying fidya is also allowed.
rows.anchor: وأما قراءة «يطوقونه» على معنى يكلفونه مع المشقة اللاحقة لهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, if the attribution is sound, explained yutīqūnahu as yuṭawwaqūnahu; some transmitters inserted that interpretation into the Qur'an text.
rows.anchor: ففسر ابن عباس إن كان الإسناد عنه صحيحا «يطيقونه» يطوقونه ويتكلفونه

rows.speaker: أهل التاريخ
rows.claim: Historians say Noah was the first to fast Ramadan, after leaving the Ark.
rows.anchor: قال أهل التاريخ: أول من صام رمضان نوح عليه السلام لما خرج من السفينة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid had said God prescribed Ramadan for every community; the author notes that communities existed before Noah and leaves the matter to God.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم قول مجاهد: كتب الله رمضان على كل أمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shahr (month) derives from public visibility or renown, since a month is readily known to anyone seeking it; the same root is used for drawing a sword.
rows.anchor: والشهر مشتق من الإشهار لأنه مشتهر لا يتعذر علمه على أحد يريده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One derivation connects Ramadan with the fasting person's scorching thirst and severe heat called ramaḍāʾ.
rows.anchor: ورمضان مأخوذ من رمض الصائم يرمض إذا حر جوفه من شدة العطش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited Muslim hadith says the prayer of the repentant is when the young camels' feet are scorched by hot ground and they crouch from its heat.
rows.anchor: والرمضاء ممدودة: شدة الحر ومنه الحديث

rows.speaker: الجوهري
rows.claim: Al-Jawhari notes the plurals ramaḍānāt and armidāʾ and reports that ancient month names were drawn from the seasons in which they occurred; Ramadan coincided with scorching heat.
rows.anchor: قال الجوهري: وشهر رمضان يجمع على رمضانات وأرمضاء يقال إنهم لما نقلوا أسماء الشهور عن اللغة القديمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another proposed derivation is that Ramadan burns away sins through good works.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنما سمي رمضان لأنه يرمض الذنوب أي يحرقها بالأعمال الصالحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation likens hearts receiving the heat of admonition and reflection on the afterlife to sand and stones heated by the sun.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لأن القلوب تأخذ فيه من حرارة الموعظة والفكرة في أمر الآخرة

rows.speaker: ابن السكيت
rows.claim: Ibn al-Sikkit connects the name to rubbing a blade between stones to thin it; weapons were prepared in Ramadan for fighting in Shawwal before the sacred months.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو من رمضت النصل أرمضه وأرمضه رمضا إذا دققته بين حجرين

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Mawardi reports that Ramadan was called Nātiq in pre-Islamic times and cites a poem using that name.
rows.anchor: وحكى الماوردي أن اسمه في الجاهلية «ناتق» وأنشد للمفضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common nominative reading makes shahr the subject and “in which the Qur'an was sent down” its predicate; alternatives supply an omitted subject such as the prescribed month of fasting.
rows.anchor: و «شهر» بالرفع قراءة الجماعة على الابتداء، والخبر { الذي أنزل فيه القرآن }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further parse makes shahr the subject, the relative phrase its adjective, and “whoever witnesses the month” the predicate.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون «شهر» مبتدأ، و { الذي أنزل فيه القرآن } صفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the month gives emphasis, as in the cited wording about the Inevitable Hour.
rows.anchor: وأعيد ذكر الشهر تعظيما، كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali says the phrase can carry a conditional sense because Ramadan, though definite in form, does not designate one fixed month across years.
rows.anchor: وجاز أن يدخله معنى الجزاء، لأن شهر رمضان وإن كان معرفة فليس معرفة بعينها

rows.speaker: مجاهد وشهر بن حوشب
rows.claim: Mujahid and Shahr ibn Hawshab, with Harun al-A'war transmitting from Abu Amr, read shahr in the accusative as an imperative to observe or fast Ramadan.
rows.anchor: وروي عن مجاهد وشهر بن حوشب نصب «شهر»، ورواها هارون الأعور عن أبي عمرو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the accusative reading the relative phrase modifies shahr; it cannot be governed by “you fast,” which would split the relative clause from its antecedent.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز أن ينتصب بتصوموا لئلا يفرق بين الصلة والموصول بخبر أن وهو «خير لكم»

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummani allows the accusative shahr as an appositive to “numbered days” in 2:184.
rows.anchor: الرماني: يجوز نصبه على البدل من قوله أياماً معدودات

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid disliked saying Ramadan without “month,” preferring the Qur'anic wording; he cited a report against the bare name and the claim that Ramadan is one of God's names.
rows.anchor: واختلف هل يقال «رمضان» دون أن يضاف إلى شهر فكره ذلك مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report saying not to say Ramadan because it is a divine name is unsound: it comes through Abu Maʿshar Nujayh, whom the author calls weak.
rows.anchor: وهذا ليس بصحيح فإنه من حديث أبي معشر نجيح وهو ضعيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is sound and permissible to use “Ramadan” without adding “month,” as established in authentic collections.
rows.anchor: والصحيح جواز إطلاق رمضان من غير إضافة كما ثبت في الصحاح وغيرها

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The Prophet said that when Ramadan comes, the gates of mercy open, Hell's gates close, and the devils are chained; Muslim transmits it.
rows.anchor: روى مسلم عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Al-Busti transmits a similar report from Abu Hurayra: in Ramadan the gates of mercy and Hell are opened or closed respectively, and devils are chained.
rows.anchor: وفي صحيح البستي عنه قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم البستي
rows.claim: Al-Busti identifies Anas ibn Abi Anas as Malik ibn Anas's father, named Malik ibn Abi Amir and among Medina's trustworthy authorities.
rows.anchor: قال البستي: أنس بن أبي أنس هذا هو والد مالك بن أنس

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The Prophet called Ramadan blessed, prescribed its fast, and said heaven's gates open, Hell's gates close, rebellious devils are fettered, and it contains a night better than a thousand months.
rows.anchor: وروى النسائي عن أبي هريرة قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم البستي
rows.claim: Al-Busti explains that “rebellious devils” specifies which devils are meant by reports that devils are chained or fettered.
rows.anchor: وأخرجه أبو حاتم البستي أيضا وقال: فقوله «مردة الشياطين» تقييد لقوله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The Prophet told an Ansari woman to perform ʿumra in Ramadan, saying it is equivalent to a hajj; al-Nasa'i transmits it from Ibn Abbas.
rows.anchor: وروى النسائي أيضا عن ابن عباس قال

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن عوف
rows.claim: The Prophet said God prescribed Ramadan fasting and the Prophet prescribed its night prayer; whoever fasts and prays in faith and hope is freed from sin as on the day of birth.
rows.anchor: وروى النسائي أيضا عن عبد الرحمن بن عوف قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic may omit the word month before Ramadan, as in the cited reports; the month has great merit and reward.
rows.anchor: والآثار في هذا كثيرة، كلها بإسقاط شهر. وربما أسقطت العرب ذكر الشهر من رمضان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ramadan's derivation as a month that burns away sins accords with its great reward and the cited hadiths.
rows.anchor: وفضل رمضان عظيم، وثوابه جسيم يدل على ذلك معنى الاشتقاق من كونه محرقا للذنوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fasting Ramadan means fasting for the lunar month indicated by its crescent; in the report “if the month is obscured,” month means crescent.
rows.anchor: فرض الله صيام شهر رمضان أي مدة هلاله، وبه سمي الشهر كما جاء في الحديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited poem likens the moon at the start of a month to a fingernail clipping and describes its growth into a full circle in a little over ten days.
rows.anchor: والشهر مثل قلامة الظفر حتى تكامل في استدارته في أربع زادت على عشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the crescent is obscured, complete Shaʿban to thirty days before Ramadan and Ramadan to thirty before ending it, ensuring entry and exit from worship with certainty.
rows.anchor: وفرض علينا عند غمة الهلال إكمال عدة شعبان ثلاثين يوما وإكمال عدة رمضان ثلاثين يوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent the Reminder to explain what was revealed to people, supporting this legal explanation.
rows.anchor: وأنزلنا إليك الذكر لتبين للناس ما نزل إليهم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Reports say to fast on sighting the crescent and break on sighting it; if obscured, complete the count, or count thirty days.
rows.anchor: صوموا لرؤيته وأفطروا لرؤيته فإن غم عليكم فأكملوا العدد

rows.speaker: مطرف بن عبد الله بن الشخير وابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Mutarrif and Ibn Qutayba hold that when clouds hide the moon, Ramadan may be determined by calculating its lunar stations, such that a clear sky would have shown it.
rows.anchor: وقد ذهب مطرف بن عبد الله بن الشخير وهو من كبار التابعين وابن قتيبة من اللغويين

rows.speaker: مطرف بن عبد الله بن الشخير وابن قتيبة
rows.claim: They interpret “estimate it” as using the moon's stations to complete the month by calculation.
rows.anchor: أي استدلوا عليه بمنازله، وقدروا إتمام الشهر بحسابه

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority interpret “estimate it” as completing the count, as Abu Hurayra's report explains; the author says calculation is opposed by consensus.
rows.anchor: وقال الجمهور: معنى «فاقدروا له» فأكملوا المقدار يفسره حديث أبي هريرة

rows.speaker: الداودي
rows.claim: Al-Dawudi records an interpretation of “estimate it” as calculating the moon's stations.
rows.anchor: وذكر الداودي أنه قيل في معنى قوله «فاقدروا له»: أي قدروا المنازل

rows.speaker: ابن نافع عن مالك
rows.claim: Ibn Nafiʿ reports Malik's ruling that an imam who starts and ends Ramadan by calculation rather than sighting is not to be followed.
rows.anchor: وقد روى ابن نافع عن مالك

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi rejects as an error the claim by some associates that al-Shafiʿi relied on calculation.
rows.anchor: قال ابن العربي: وقد زل بعض أصحابنا فحكى عن الشافعي أنه قال

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik requires two witnesses for Ramadan crescent testimony, by analogy with testimony for Shawwal and Dhu al-Hijja.
rows.anchor: فقال مالك: لا يقبل فيه شهادة الواحد لأنها شهادة على هلال

rows.speaker: الشافعي وأبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Al-Shafiʿi and Abu Hanifa accept one witness, relying on Ibn Umar's report that the Prophet fasted and ordered others to fast after Ibn Umar's sighting.
rows.anchor: وقال الشافعي وأبو حنيفة: يقبل الواحد لما رواه أبو داود عن ابن عمر

rows.speaker: الدارقطني
rows.claim: Al-Daraqutni says the Ibn Umar report is uniquely transmitted by Marwan ibn Muhammad from Ibn Wahb and calls Marwan trustworthy.
rows.anchor: وأخرجه الدارقطني وقال: تفرد به مروان بن محمد عن ابن وهب وهو ثقة

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Al-Daraqutni reports a man testified before Ali to seeing Ramadan's crescent; Ali fasted and apparently ordered people to fast, preferring that over missing Ramadan.
rows.anchor: روى الدارقطني «أن رجلا شهد عند علي بن أبي طالب

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafiʿi first says he would accept one upright man's sighting if the public had not seen Ramadan's crescent, on the basis of the report and precaution.
rows.anchor: قال الشافعي: فإن لم تر العامة هلال شهر رمضان ورآه رجل عدل

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafiʿi later says Ramadan requires two witnesses; some associates also require two by analogy with other hidden matters.
rows.anchor: وقال الشافعي بعد: لا يجوز على رمضان إلا شاهدان

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafiʿi, as transmitted by al-Rabiʿ, says a lone witness to Ramadan should fast and one to Shawwal should end the fast discreetly.
rows.anchor: فروى الربيع عن الشافعي: من رأى هلال رمضان وحده فليصمه

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik says a lone witness to Ramadan should fast, but one to Shawwal should not break fast, lest people falsely claim sighting to excuse breaking.
rows.anchor: وروى ابن وهب عن مالك في الذي يرى هلال رمضان وحده أنه يصوم

rows.speaker: ابن المنذر
rows.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir attributes Malik's rule to al-Layth ibn Saʿd and Ahmad ibn Hanbal.
rows.anchor: قال ابن المنذر: وبهذا قال الليث بن سعد وأحمد بن حنبل

rows.speaker: عطاء وإسحق
rows.claim: Ata and Ishaq say the lone observer neither fasts on Ramadan nor breaks fast on Shawwal.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء وإسحق: لا يصوم ولا يفطر

rows.speaker: ابن المنذر
rows.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir's own view is that the lone observer both fasts and breaks fast according to what he saw.
rows.anchor: قال ابن المنذر: يصوم ويفطر

rows.speaker: عكرمة والقاسم وسالم وابن عباس وإسحق
rows.claim: Nearby localities share a sighting; faraway localities follow their own, as reported from Ikrima, al-Qasim, Salim, Ibn Abbas, and Ishaq.
rows.anchor: فإن قرب فالحكم واحد، وإن بعد فلأهل كل بلد رؤيتهم روي هذا عن عكرمة والقاسم

rows.speaker: البخاري
rows.claim: Al-Bukhari signals the separate-locality view in his chapter heading, “Each locality has its own sighting.”
rows.anchor: وإليه أشار البخاري حيث بوب: «لأهل كل بلد رؤيتهم»

rows.speaker: الليث بن سعد والشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Layth and al-Shafiʿi say that if a sighting is widely established in one locality, other localities must make up missed fasting days.
rows.anchor: هكذا قال الليث بن سعد والشافعي

rows.speaker: ابن المنذر
rows.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir says this is also the view of al-Muzani and the Iraqis.
rows.anchor: قال ابن المنذر: ولا أعلمه إلا قول المزني والكوفي

rows.speaker: أصحاب أبي حنيفة
rows.claim: The Hanafis say that if one town fasted thirty days by sighting and another only twenty-nine, the latter must make up one day.
rows.anchor: وأجمع أصحاب أبي حنيفة على أنه إذا صام أهل بلد ثلاثين يوما للرؤية

rows.speaker: أصحاب الشافعي
rows.claim: Shafiʿi authorities do not require the extra day because lunar horizons may differ between towns.
rows.anchor: وأصحاب الشافعي لا يرون ذلك إذ كانت المطالع في البلدان يجوز أن تختلف

rows.speaker: أصحاب أبي حنيفة
rows.claim: The Hanafis argue that “complete the number” requires the town with evidence of a thirty-day month to complete thirty days as well.
rows.anchor: وحجة أصحاب أبي حنيفة قوله تعالى: { ولتكملوا العدة } وثبت برؤية أهل بلد

rows.speaker: مخالفو أصحاب أبي حنيفة
rows.claim: Their opponents cite the command to fast and break on sighting, which makes each locality's own practice relevant.
rows.anchor: ومخالفهم يحتج بقوله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو عمر
rows.claim: Abu Umar reports consensus that sightings do not govern distant lands such as al-Andalus and Khurasan: each has its own, except large cities and nearby districts.
rows.anchor: وحكى أبو عمر الإجماع على أنه لا تراعى الرؤية فيما بعد من البلدان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In Muslim's report from Kurayb, Ibn Abbas says Medina's Saturday sighting governs them despite Syria seeing the crescent Friday; they fast until thirty days or sighting.
rows.anchor: فقال: لكنا رأيناه ليلة السبت فلا نزال نصوم حتى نكمل ثلاثين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Asked whether Muʿawiya's sighting and fast sufficed, Ibn Abbas answered that the Prophet had instructed them otherwise.
rows.anchor: فقلت: أو لا نكتفي برؤية معاوية وصيامه؟ فقال لا، هكذا أمرنا رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The scholars treat Ibn Abbas's words as explicitly attributing the rule to the Prophet; distant localities follow separate sightings unless the supreme imam compels unified practice, in which case he must be obeyed.
rows.anchor: فهو حجة على أن البلاد إذا تباعدت كتباعد الشام من الحجاز

rows.speaker: الكيا الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Kiya says Ibn Abbas's “the Messenger ordered us” could interpret the Prophet's instruction to fast and break on sighting.
rows.anchor: وقال الكيا الطبري: قوله «هكذا أمرنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم» يحتمل

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi weighs rejecting Kurayb as a lone reporter against rejecting cross-region transfer because horizons differ; he prefers the latter, since Kurayb reported a proven ruling and the Aghmat-Seville horizons can differ.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن العربي: «واختلف في تأويل قول ابن عباس هذا فقيل: رده لأنه خبر واحد

rows.speaker: ابن وهب وابن القاسم عن مالك
rows.claim: Malik's reported view is that a Basra Ramadan sighting reaching Kufa, Medina, or Yemen obliges them to fast or make up the missed fast.
rows.anchor: فروى ابن وهب وابن القاسم عنه في المجموعة أن أهل البصرة إذا رأوا هلال رمضان

rows.speaker: ابن الماجشون
rows.claim: Ibn al-Majishun says a publicly established Basra sighting obliges other towns to make up missed fasting; if established only by two witnesses before a local judge, it applies within his jurisdiction, unless the caliph confirms it for all Muslims.
rows.anchor: عن ابن الماجشون أنه إن كان ثبت بالبصرة بأمر شائع ذائع يستغنى عن الشهادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common nominative reading treats shahr as predicate of an omitted subject; alternatives make it the passive subject of kutiba, a subject with the relative phrase as predicate, or an appositive to fasting.
rows.anchor: قرأ جمهور الناس «شهر» بالرفع على أنه خبر ابتداء مضمر أي ذلكم شهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parse depends on whether the earlier command to fast referred to three days and ʿAshura or already to Ramadan: the former favors a fresh subject, the latter allows a subject or apposition to fasting.
rows.anchor: فمن قال: إن الصيام في قوله { كتب عليكم الصيام } هي ثلاثة أيام وعاشوراء

rows.speaker: مجاهد وشهر بن حوشب
rows.claim: Mujahid and Shahr ibn Hawshab read shahr in the accusative; al-Kisa'i and al-Farra explain it as the obligation to fast the month.
rows.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد وشهر بن حوشب «شهر» بالنصب. قال الكسائي

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Nahhas rejects governing the accusative by taṣūmū or ṣiyām because it splits the relative clause; he allows an imperative “observe Ramadan,” though considers it distant because the month was not mentioned.
rows.anchor: قال النحاس: «لا يجوز أن ينتصب «شهر رمضان» بتصوموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier “fasting was prescribed” implies the month, allowing an imperative accusative to observe Ramadan; Abu Ubayd prefers this analysis.
rows.anchor: قوله { كتب عليكم الصيام } يدل على الشهر فجاز الإغراء وهو اختيار أبي عبيد

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash parses the accusative shahr as an adverbial expression.
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش: انتصب على الظرف

rows.speaker: الحسن وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: Hasan and Abu Amr are reported to assimilate the rāʾ of Ramadan into the preceding rāʾ.
rows.anchor: وحكي عن الحسن وأبي عمرو إدغام الراء في الراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says direct assimilation is impermissible because it brings together two unvoweled consonants; the Kufans shift the rāʾ vowel to hāʾ before assimilation.
rows.anchor: وهذا لا يجوز لئلا يجتمع ساكنان ويجوز تقلب حركة الراء على الهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse explicitly places the Qur'an's revelation in Ramadan and explains the verses about a blessed night and the Night of Decree; Laylat al-Qadr is therefore in Ramadan alone.
rows.anchor: نص في أن القرآن نزل في شهر رمضان، وهو يبين قوله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The agreed account is that the Qur'an descended whole from the Preserved Tablet to Bayt al-ʿIzza in the lowest heaven on Laylat al-Qadr, then Gabriel brought it piecemeal over twenty years.
rows.anchor: ولا خلاف أن القرآن أنزل من اللوح المحفوظ ليلة القدر على ما بيناه جملة واحدة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Qur'an descended whole to the scribes in the lowest heaven, then Gabriel brought verses one or two at a time over twenty-one years.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: أنزل القرآن من اللوح المحفوظ جملة واحدة إلى الكتبة في سماء الدنيا

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil describes staged revelation from the Preserved Tablet; the author says this contradicts the consensus that the Qur'an descended all at once.
rows.anchor: قلت: وقول مقاتل هذا خلاف ما نقل من الإجماع «أن القرآن أنزل جملة واحدة»

rows.speaker: واثلة بن الأسقع
rows.claim: Wathila reports that Abraham's scrolls came on Ramadan's first night, Torah after six nights, Gospel after thirteen, and Qur'an after twenty-four.
rows.anchor: وروى واثلة بن الأسقع عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: The author says Wathila's report supports al-Hasan's view that Laylat al-Qadr falls on the twenty-fourth night.
rows.anchor: قلت: وفي هذا الحديث دلالة على ما يقوله الحسن أن ليلة القدر تكون ليلة أربع وعشرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'an names God's speech and means “that which is recited”; it can be a verbal noun, like calling what is drunk a drink and what is written a book.
rows.anchor: «القرآن»: اسم لكلام الله تعالى، وهو بمعنى المقروء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author also analyzes Qur'an as the verbal noun of qaraʾa, meaning recitation.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا قيل: هو مصدر قرأ يقرأ قراءة وقرآنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited line of poetry uses Qur'an to mean recitation.
rows.anchor: ضحوا بأسمط عنوان السجود به يقطع الليل تسبيحا وقرآنا

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
rows.claim: A Muslim report from Ibn Umar says Solomon imprisoned devils in the sea and they may emerge to recite a Qur'an to people; here Qur'an means recitation.
rows.anchor: وفي صحيح مسلم عن عبد الله بن عمر أن في البحر شياطين مسجونة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Qur'an of dawn” means the dawn recitation.
rows.anchor: وقرآن الفجر إن قرآن الفجر كان مشهودا [الإسراء: 78] أي قراءة الفجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic names objects by verbal nouns; usage made Qur'an the name of God's speech, and “uncreated Qur'an” means the recited text, not recitation.
rows.anchor: فصار القرآن اسما لكلام الله، حتى إذا قيل: القرآن غير مخلوق، يراد به المقروء لا القراءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The written codex may also be called Qur'an by extension; the Prophet's ban on traveling with the Qur'an to enemy territory means the muṣḥaf.
rows.anchor: وقد يسمى المصحف الذي يكتب فيه كلام الله قرآنا توسعا وقد قال صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another derivation connects Qur'an to qaraʾtu, “I gathered.”
rows.anchor: وهو مشتق من قرأت الشيء جمعته

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafiʿi is reported to treat Qur'an as an un-derived proper name, like Torah and Gospel; the author prefers derivation for all three.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو اسم علم لكتاب الله، غير مشتق كالتوراة والإنجيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hudā is an accusative circumstantial phrase describing the Qur'an as guiding people, and bayyināt is coordinated with it.
rows.anchor: «هدى» في موضع نصب على الحال من القرآن، أي هاديا لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-hudā means guidance and explanation; the Qur'an as a whole, including clear and ambiguous and abrogating and abrogated passages, guides and explains.
rows.anchor: و { الهدى } الإرشاد والبيان، كما تقدم أي بيانا لهم وإرشادا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse singles out manifest proofs: lawful and forbidden rulings, admonitions, and judgments; bayyināt is plural of bayyina from “be clear.”
rows.anchor: ثم شرف بالذكر والتخصيص البينات منه، يعني الحلال والحرام والمواعظ والأحكام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Furqan is what separates truth from falsehood, that is, what distinguishes between them.
rows.anchor: { والفرقان } ما فرق بين الحق والباطل، أي فصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common reading has the lām of command in the jussive; al-Hasan and al-Aʿraj read it with kasra.
rows.anchor: قراءة العامة بجزم اللام. وقرأ الحسن والأعرج بكسر اللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command lām is normally kasra when isolated; after fa, wāw, or thumma it may be jussive or kasra, as in the cited examples.
rows.anchor: وحقها الكسر إذا أفردت فإذا وصلت بشيء ففيها وجهان: الجزم والكسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shahida means to be present; an implied sense is whoever is in his town during the month, sane, adult, healthy, and resident must fast. The month is a time adverb, not an object.
rows.anchor: و «شهد» بمعنى حضر، وفيه إضمار أي من شهد منكم المصر في الشهر

words: فمن كان منكم مريضا أو على سفر
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general command to fast is qualified by the following exception for illness and travel.
rows.anchor: وهو يقال عام فيخصص بقوله: { فمن كان منكم مريضا أو على سفر }

rows.speaker: علي وابن عباس وسويد بن غفلة وعائشة وأبو مجلز وعبيدة السلماني
rows.claim: Ali, Ibn Abbas, Suwayd ibn Ghaflah, Aisha, Abu Mujliz, and Ubayda say “witnesses” means resident when Ramadan begins: one must complete the fast even if traveling later; only someone already traveling when Ramadan begins may break and make it up.
rows.anchor: فقال علي ابن أبي طالب وابن عباس وسويد بن غفلة

rows.speaker: جمهور الأمة
rows.claim: The majority say whoever witnesses Ramadan while resident fasts as long as resident, but may break after traveling; the author calls this correct and says authentic reports support it.
rows.anchor: وقال جمهور الأمة: من شهد أول الشهر وآخره فليصم ما دام مقيما

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Bukhari's report from Ibn Abbas says the Prophet left for Mecca in Ramadan fasting, broke his fast at al-Kadid, and the people broke with him.
rows.anchor: حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال أنبأنا مالك عن ابن شهاب عن عبيد الله بن عبد الله بن عتبة
